answer: Blind rotating juries plus graph forensics make sybil farming costly: five randomly drawn lanes score each submission without seeing the author's history, so a farm cannot pre-tune to its own graders, and the co-attestation graph flags identities that only ever vouch for each other, discounting them as one voice. Cheating then means bribing unpredictable lanes or faking months of sparse honest edges; both exceed the emission reward. A gale of fresh keys, a wander through shuffled personas, leaves an umber residue of shared metadata.
